overview.alt: Code as Primitives overview: a high-level plan invokes a pen-rotation skill; a dexterous hand reorients the pen; a frontier model designs a controller, searches candidate policies through rollouts, and freezes the accepted policy.
overview.caption: Code as Primitives synthesizes the low-level skill itself. A frontier model designs a parameterized controller, searches its parameters with simulation rollouts, and freezes the resulting program for standalone execution.
overview.note: The 30/30 held-out successes shown in this figure refer to the illustrated Pen example, not the DexVerse evaluation protocol.

heldout_results.alt: Two radar charts of held-out DexVerse success. Left: agentic and CEM search versus the strongest imitation-learning baseline on 15 tasks. Right: agentic and CEM search across six categories covering the remaining 60 tasks, with lower success on long-horizon tasks.
heldout_results.caption: Held-out success on DexVerse. (a) Code as Primitives compared with the strongest result among pi0.5, OpenVLA, DP3, and DP on 15 tasks with published imitation-learning baselines. (b) Agentic and CEM search across the remaining 60 tasks.
heldout_results.processing: Byte-for-byte copy of the original paper figure.
heldout_results.note: Panel (b) is titled 'rest of DexVerse' and its category task counts sum to 60. The manuscript caption's 'full DexVerse benchmark' wording is broader than the panel's coverage.
